description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for the centered nonuniform first-derivative rule central_D1_nonuniform_dirichlet_bc (the rule under test, advective term) driven by problems/advection_1d_nonuniform_dirichlet.esm on the quadratic-stretch mesh (b=0.4); the diffusive term uses central_D2_nonuniform_dirichlet_bc, whose physical dissipation makes the two-sided fixed-value problem well posed (a pure-advection two-sided Dirichlet driver is GKS-unstable and does NOT converge). The problem file is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding of N (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4); the consumer re-derives the x-shaped geometry observeds xc and dxw from N at each resolution. The exact unforced solution e^{2x} + e^{-lambda t} e^{x} sin(pi x) (steady mode plus decaying first Dirichlet eigenfunction, shared walls gL=1, gR=e^2) gives a discrete drift that is pure spatial-discretization error at t=0.05, dominated by the advective D1 term. The gate checks the L2 norm ONLY: the centered nonuniform operator with second-order fixed-value Dirichlet walls is second-order in L2 by supraconvergence even though the interior pointwise truncation is O(h) where the spacing varies (LeVeque 2007 section 2.13); a broken/first-order D1 closure would degrade the order below 2, so this is a real order test of the rule.
